articleTitle: Bio composite materials: nano functionalization of 4D bio engineered scaffold
abstract: The combination of 3D bioprinting techniques and low-cost portable spectrophotometer allows the development of "bio-composite materials" that is shape-memory functionalized scaffolds with a uniform distribution of ultrafine material.

articleTitle: Optical Flow Sensor for Lung Surfactant Delivery
abstract: Respiratory distress syndrome is a major cause of death of preterm newborns. This is due to the absence of lung surfactant. Non-invasive medical cares are in development, which need to know in real time the flow of surfactant instilled in the newborn. This work proposes the use of an optical flow sensor based on self-mixing interferometry. A dedicated prototype is realized for measuring surfactant flow rate in a small diameter duct, and its performances are evaluated.

articleTitle: Line-scanning two-photon microscope for the investigation of biological samples
abstract: We present a novel two-photon microscope employing a line-scanning technique that allows image acquisition at a high rate. The resolution turns out to be comparable to the one of common point-scanning systems.

articleTitle: High Sensitive Microsurgical Force Sensor Using Spectral-Width of Tapered Fiber Bragg Gratings
abstract: Theoretical and numerical simulation show that the location of the Bragg gratings within the fused tapered fiber improves the axial force sensitivity/minimizes the transversal forces effect during tissue-needle interaction in vitreoretinal microsurgical (VRMS) procedure.

articleTitle: A novel technique for the measurement of twophoton absorption spectra of dyes for nonlinear fluorescence microscopy
abstract: We present a novel technique for the measurement of two-photon absorption spectra. A line-shaped excitation beam generates a strong induced fluorescence signal that can be easily detected by an image sensor.

articleTitle: Signal Processing in Stimulated Emission Microscopy
abstract: In this paper, signal processing through various modulation techniques in stimulated emission (SE) microscopy are described. In addition, background free, improvement of signal-to-noise ratio, and high speed SE imaging modalities are demonstrated.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Approach for Red Blood Cell Segmentation from Full-Field OCT Data of Human Skin
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to segment red blood cells from the Full-Field OCT data of human skin, using deep learning technique. Test results show the developed technique is very promising for real time detection and counting of red blood cells.

articleTitle: Spectroscopic Full-field Optical Coherence Tomography in Dermatology
abstract: Full-field optical coherence tomography with ultra-precise positioning of the PZT by polynomial hysteresis compensation enables depth-dependent spectral data extraction from raw OCT interferometric data. Spectral analysis could quantify molecular/chemical composition of the tissue constituents.

articleTitle: Characterisation of a DNA hydrogel viscosity by an integrated optofluidic microrheometer
abstract: Here we present a novel microrheometer able to provide reliable measurements of extremely low volume fluids. We demonstrate the transition from Newtonian to non-Newtonian behavior in a DNA hydrogel whose structure is strongly temperature dependent.

In this work, we have demonstrated polarization resolved pump-probe stimulated emission (SE) measurements. Impotently, we realized depolarization effect by resolving anisotropy fluorescence lifetime through pump-probe SE microscopy. This technique is cost effective and robust.

articleTitle: Deep Feature Learning for Contour Segmentation of Aorta's Intima by Using Sub-Micron-Resolution OCT
abstract: Deep learning algorithm is applied on the optical coherence tomographic images of the tunica intima of rat's aorta to segment its boundary. With the cellular resolution, an average boundary error of 0.49 um was achieved.

articleTitle: A 180-nm Tunable Ti:sapphire Crystal Fiber Laser for OCT Applications
abstract: Thanks to a Ti:sapphire crystal fiber grown in our Laboratories, we develop a diode-pumped, 25-mW tunable laser with a 180-nm tuning range. The CF is 2.4-cm long and has an elliptical core with 13/15-μm diameter in the [0001/1100] axes and is cladded with silica. A blazed grating provides wavelength tuning a continuous tuning range of laser emission from 700 to 880 nm, with a slope efficiency of 6.1%.

articleTitle: The Single Software Architecture Supporting Fourier Domain Optical Coherence Tomography System
abstract: We developed a software architecture utilizing the MFC library, allowing OCT imaging/data acquisition in a synchronized fashion. This architecture supports both version of the Fourier-domain OCT frameworks, including the spectral-domain and the swept-source OCT.

articleTitle: Near-Infrared Transillumination of in Vivo Biological Tissues for Functional Imaging
abstract: The following topics are dealt with: biomedical optical imaging; optical tomography; optical microscopy; medical image processing; image resolution; biological techniques; stimulated emission; biological tissues; cardiology; and image segmentation.

articleTitle: Neurite Retraction and Regrowth under Optical and Chemical Stimulations
abstract: We demonstrated that 473 nm blue light caused the neurite retraction in mouse neuroblastoma cell N2a, while 650 nm red light induced neurite regrowth. The myosin II inhibitor blebbistatin enhanced this red light-induced neurite regeneration. We also observed the actin wave propagating from the soma to the tip of a re-growing neurite. This red light-induced neurite regrowth did not occur in the calcium-free culture medium.

articleTitle: Fast Gate Synchronized Subharmonic Modulation in Stimulated Emission Microscopy
abstract: In this paper, an alternative modulation technique working at much higher frequency (38 MHz) is demonstrated for stimulated emission microscopy. In this way, shot noise limited sensitivity and high speed imaging can be achieved.

articleTitle: Lissajous Scanning Microscopy Using Tailored Optical Fibre
abstract: This paper reports the development of optical fibre scanner using dual-core multi-mode fibre for imaging biological sample. The fibre is driven with non-repeating Lissajous scan pattern. The reconstructed image from a barcode and granule Saccharomyces Cerevisiae is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Progress in Interferometric Measurements of Biological Signals
abstract: Interferometric techniques have been demonstrated valuable in a number of different experiments involving the measurement of biological signals, because they provide unparalleled sensitivity, contactless operation and are applicable to a variety of biological signals involving kinematic measurands. In particular, self-mixing interferometry (SMI) is attracting interest because of the very simple experimental setup and low cost. We discuss recent progresses of SMI in the field of vibrometry, pressure waves and flow, and THz detection.

articleTitle: Cheap, smart and reliable technology for biosensors and diagnostics tools
abstract: In this study single-board computers, like Raspberry Pi, assembled with inexpensive opto-electronic components have been used to realize smart and friendlyinterface diagnostic tools which have been successfully tested and compared with more expensive and complicated lab equipment like a spectrophotometer. A dedicated python software and a wireless connection with smartphone or tablet provides the data processing and the analysis control. This approach has the potentiality for portable and reliable diagnostics and opens new opportunities in research and education.
